newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA officials face eight lawsuits.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA officials face eight lawsuits.

text.p: Eight separate shareholder lawsuits have been filed against officials of Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp. in U.S. District Court in Nashville, Tenn., since a massive federal probe of the company began in March.

The most recent was filed Tuesday by Zwerling Schachter & Zwerling, a New York law firm representing shareholders who allege misconduct by certain key officials of the company, said the court's civil clerk's office.

The clerk's office said seven similar actions have been filed since April 8 -- three weeks after Nashville, Tenn.-based Columbia/HCA said its El Paso, Texas operations were served with search warrants by federal agents.
A federal investigation of the largest U.S. for-profit hospital company has since spread to six states and caused a sharp drop in the value of Columbia/HCA's stock.
Shares in the company recovered early Wednesday, however, as rumors flew that it may be in merger talks and that its chief executive officer may face a possible ouster.

The Wall Street Journal Wednesday quoted people familiar with the situation as saying Columbia/HCA is in discussions with Tenet HealthCare Corp, the second-largest U.S. for-profit hospital company, about a possible combination.

In a separate development, The Tennesseean newspaper in Nashville Wednesday quoted an unnamed source as saying Columbia/HCA's board members in a special telephone meeting on Saturday discussed concerns about long-time chairman and chief executive Richard Scott.
"I think we're going to be sitting here in the low 30s for some time ... I just don't see how Columbia's stock can outperform the market over the next six months, a year or longer," Villwock said.

Federal agents last week seized records relating to laboratory billing and home healthcare operations at Columbia/HCA facilities in Florida, Texas, Tennessee, North Carolina, Oklahoma and Utah, the company said.
Five Columbia/HCA mid-level executives in Florida have been subpoenaed to testify to a grand jury in connection with the probe, the company said.
Separate inquiries into company business activities are being pursued by the attorneys general of Texas and Alabama.
Columbia/HCA had 1996 revenues of $19.9 billion. It runs 342 hospitals, 150 surgery centers and more than 570 home health locations in 36 states, England, Switzerland and Spain.
